source.title: Unlearning by Extrapolating a Shrink-and-Heal Lookahead

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests relearning attacks on unlearned models and proposes S HIFT as a more attack-robust counter-method. Its results refine the claim: recovery and distance to the attacked oracle vary by method and attack strength.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for related-data fine-tuning attacks (Tables 10–11). It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery. The main unlearning tables report performance and utility, but not near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy as required by version A.
record.test_reason: The study runs a relearning attack on 12 unlearned Llama-3.2-1B models (TOFU forget05): fine-tune on half the forget authors, test on the held-out half (Appendix G, Tables 10–11). This bears on B for the existing baselines and on F for its own method S HIFT. Most baselines recover little or nothing beyond the equally attacked oracle, so for B the results mostly qualify or challenge the version rather than confirm it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that likelihood-suppression unlearning has no target, so its outcome follows the optimization budget. They argue S HIFT, which targets an estimate of the retrain oracle, ends closest to the oracle with the best average aggregate score. On relearning, they report S HIFT within 0.008 of the equally attacked oracle and closest at all six strengths. They say aggressive forgetting bounces back (RMU ES 0.029 to 0.195), and that stronger attacks erode the Full model, moving every method toward the oracle.
record.recipe_differences: S HIFT is a new shrink-and-heal lookahead and distillation method, not a reproduction of the original unlearning methods. Its attack evaluation fine-tunes on half of the forget authors and tests on the other half.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning attack learning rate and number of epochs change the reported distance to the equally attacked oracle; results are reported at attack learning rates 10−5 and 2·10−5 and one to three epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Likelihood-suppression baselines over-forget past the retrain oracle as the learning rate grows: privacy leakage reaches +40 to +57 at 5e-5 for all but SimNPO (Fig. 1a, Table 7). S HIFT stays within [-23, +6] from 2e-5 up.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How far unlearning forgets is set by the optimization budget, and methods can over-forget beyond the retrain oracle, which is detectable by membership inference.

record.problems: The relearning evaluation uses one model size and one TOFU split. Attack results are means of three seeds, but no error bars are given. The attack data are related forget-set examples, and results are measured on held-out authors; the study does not test unrelated-data relearning or the other attack families in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix G, Table 11 reports 72 method-by-attack-strength distance values. To stay within the 60-row limit, this record includes all six S HIFT values, all six RMU values highlighted for rebound, and the closest baseline at each attack strength; the other baseline-method cells from Table 11 are omitted. Table 10's separate ES and RL outcomes are retained for all listed methods.

untested.parts: Entire version. TOFU Mem/Util are reported, but not near-chance targeted accuracy together with robustness to simple attacks.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; larger relearning sets; hazardous-knowledge benchmarks such as WMDP; models other than Llama-3.2-1B; splits other than forget05.
Entire version: no activation ablation and no blocking-versus-deletion analysis of existing methods.
Entire version: no prompting, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
S HIFT's robustness to quantization, activation edits and prompting attacks; relearning at other model sizes and splits.

missing.what: The unlearning-rate context for the attacked models. They were unlearned at 2e-5, where RMU (PL +50), GradDiff (+49) and PDU (+14) over-forget. RMU's rebound therefore starts from an over-forgotten state.

record.verdict_notes: Recovery should be judged against the equally attacked oracle (ES 0.070, RL 0.353) and attacked Full (ES 0.316, RL 0.537), not against Full before the attack. The attack lowers even the Full model's held-out knowledge, so it is weak and odd as a relearning probe. SimNPO and SatImp barely forgot, so their drops are not reversals. The S HIFT rows were moved from B to F. The T11 baseline cells were chosen as the closest baseline and record absolute distances with no direction. One model (1B), one split, three attack seeds, no error bars. The paper is from the record's authors and is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates unlearning and retained utility, but does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy together with an attack test under that criterion.
Tests fine-tuning on half of the TOFU forget05 authors and evaluates the other half; does not test unrelated examples, other relearning datasets, or other attack types.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether an existing method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge. The paper's theoretical analysis concerns S HIFT's shrink-and-heal method.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language-switching, or prompting-only recovery test.
S HIFT is evaluated against related-data fine-tuning attacks only, not against activation edits, quantization, or prompting attacks.
